newsitem.title: UK: Seamus Heaney wins Britain's Whitbread prize.
newsitem.headline: Seamus Heaney wins Britain's Whitbread prize.

text.p: Seamus Heaney won the Whitbread Book of the Year award, one of Britain's most prestigious literary prizes, for his latest volume of poetry on Tuesday.
The Irish poet captured the 21,000 pound ($34,880) prize for "The Spirit Level", his first book of poems since he won the 1995 Nobel Prize for Literature.

Heaney's work was selected from a shortlist of four titles which had won 2,000 pounds each in their individual categories. He beat bookmakers' favourite Beryl Bainbridge, who was nominated for "Every Man for Himself", a tale about the sinking of the Titanic.
"It was a tightly fought final and the decision of the nine judges was not unanimous," said Malcolm Bradbury, chairman of the judging panel.
"Heaney is not only a Nobel Prize winner but he represents some of the most powerful, original and energetic work in the language," he added.

The Northern Ireland born writer, who lives in Dublin, has been hailed as Ireland's greatest poet since W.B. Yeats. When he won the Whitbread Poetry Award earlier this month one of the judges said, "It confirms Seamus Heaney's reputation as one fo the greatest poets working in the English language."
The other finalists were John Lanchester for "The Debt to Pleasure," his first novel, and Diarmaid MacCulloch for "Thomas Cranmer: A Life".
